specification_anchor_refs.verbatim: [GUI-DESKTOP-022] The chosen renderer MUST preserve native window/input, keyboard/focus/IME, DPI, accessibility, multiwindow, resize/minimize/restore and required surface/device recovery behavior.

Vulkan acceptance MUST identify the actual backend and device on the exact running application binary/source/dependency/configuration and bind evidence to genuine rendered frames and the affected lifecycle actions.
An asset-local test host (for example a harness binary) is permitted for asset proof only and is never acceptance evidence for the product.

closure_unit.outcome: One zero-egui x64 Windows test binary, built from the MT-203 GPU owner, the MT-214 and MT-215 crates and one pinned Kumihimo revision, passes eleven measured checks on an x64 desktop PC, or fails with a recorded cause and the Masonry-core fallback review opens. Docking work on the new shell stays closed until a validator PASS.

materialized_acceptance.text: Closure: the x64 gate binary's normal dependency closure contains none of egui, eframe, egui-winit, egui-wgpu, egui_tiles, epaint, ecolor, emath, egui_kittest, kumihimo-egui, cabinet-egui, cabinet-peak-egui, handshake_context_menu_egui, wgpu, wgpu-core, wgpu-hal, glow, and the only vkCreateInstance/vkCreateDevice caller in the process is the MT-203 owner (checked by a counting seam and by source scan).

Text field with IME: Japanese and Chinese composition shows the preedit underlined at the caret with the candidate window at the caret rectangle, commits once, cancels without inserting, and survives focus loss. Event-scripted in a quiet window, plus one Operator-typed pass with the real OS IME (HBR-QUIET-004).

Scroll: a 100,000-line document scrolls continuously at 1920x1080 and 100% scale; every measured frame after 60 warm-up frames has CPU record+submit plus GPU time (timestamp queries, present wait excluded) within 8.33 ms. Report p50, p99, max and frame count.

Accessibility: an out-of-process UIA client reads names, roles, bounds, values and focus, invokes the button and sets the field value, while the window is never activated; foreground window, focus and Z-order of other windows are identical before and after.

CJK and RTL: a fixed corpus of Japanese, Chinese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew, mixed bidi, combining marks and emoji renders through the fallback chain; caret stops, word motion, hit test, selection rectangles and grapheme deletion equal the recorded expected values; a missing glyph is visible and diagnosed, never silent.

Argus: argus.inspect returns the live tree with bounds and viewport source; argus.click and argus.set_value produce receipts and the observed effect; argus.screenshot returns an offscreen or swapchain-image Vulkan readback of the presented frame for root and detached windows, never an OS screen grab.

Detached window: a second OS window shares the one device, moves a view and back without losing its identity, focus rule or IME state, follows per-monitor DPI, and closes without releasing in-flight work.

Device loss: a controlled loss yields the typed outcome, MT-203 rebind and redraw of the same state; charges are not refunded; repeated failure shows a typed unavailable state with no fallback backend.

Idle: with no input for 60 s the shell submits no GPU work except a visible caret blink, the UI-thread heartbeat advances at least every 250 ms, and Palmistry reports Healthy; an owned 6 s UI-thread block yields Suspected or Frozen plus a survivor record, then recovery.

Memory: every allocation is charged to an MT-203 claim; after 100 open/close cycles of the detached window and after shutdown, usage_by_module returns to the recorded baseline with zero double release.

Platform: results count only from an x64 desktop PC with a discrete or desktop GPU; CPU architecture, GPU, driver, Vulkan version, Windows build, monitor and scale are in the receipt. ARM64 (Adreno) results are labelled not acceptance.

implementation_steps.step: S1 (first coding slice): create the crate with its own [workspace], Cargo.lock and a shell-gate binary that writes a JSON receipt (machine identity, package revisions, check list all NOT_RUN); add the closure test that fails on the banned list. No window, no GPU.
S2: open the MT-203 owner, admit one claim, record device identity, settle, close; typed unavailable path exercised.
S3: quiet window plus swapchain through MT-214; clear, present, resize, minimize, restore; damage-driven loop with submit counters.
S4: draw one Kumihimo display list on the injected device and compare readback with the CPU painter of the same list.
S5: text field, 100,000-line virtual list, button and a small tree; IME port; CJK/RTL corpus check.
S6: accessibility adapter and an out-of-process UIA client with a focus and Z-order audit around it.
S7: Argus ports: inspect, click, set_value, screenshot by Vulkan readback.
S8: detached window, per-monitor DPI change, controlled device loss, 100 open/close cycles.
S9: idle heartbeat with Palmistry attached; owned freeze.
S10: one command per check (shell-gate --check <name> --receipt <path>) so a validator can run each alone.

hbr_obligations.obligation_or_reason: The gate is an asset-local style test host: it proves feasibility and is never product acceptance.
Each control and action declared once with a stable id that feeds GUI, AccessKit, Argus and UserManual.
All GPU work through the MT-203 owner: admission, budget, retained accounting, exactly-once release, typed loss.
Every cache, queue and buffer bounded and accounted, with overload, cancel, stale-revision and release behaviour.
GUI actions, states, errors and GPU failures through the existing internal_diagnostics allowlist, content-free.
Heartbeat and owned freeze on the gate binary; product crash survival stays with MT-202 AC202-7 and AC202-9.
Every command carries actor/session, command id, revision and correlation; correlation grants nothing.
Focus, IME, AccessKit, DPI, multiwindow and recovery; docking is outside this gate.
Validator drives the running surface through Argus (stable author_id, no foreground).
Renderer error scan on every captured frame: Vulkan validation messages and runtime errors; any error fails.
Capture matrix: normal, constrained viewport, and empty/error/loading/multi-item states.
Trace projection where there is no direct surface.
A surface Argus cannot see or steer is repaired in this MT or recorded as a blocking gap.
Automated runs use a quiet, never-activated window or offscreen frame; zero focus or Z-order change.
No OS input injection, cursor movement or foregrounding on any path, tests included.
Background launches record owner and are reclaimed; no orphan windows or processes.
A step that needs the foreground (real OS IME typing) is declared first and run by the Operator.
Three-tier diagnostic outcome recorded per tier (hbr_int_009_tier_obligations).
One owning module in execution.module_ref; write scope derives from its roots; dependency direction stated.
Warm rebuild time and relinked test binaries recorded for the candidate.
Mechanic consumed from its single existing owner (context_capsule.consumed_capability_refs).
No new canonical mechanic without a spec primitive and an owner search.
Accountable owner and independently selectable source, dependency, build, test and artifact closure.
Exact embedding adapter; host policy stays in Handshake.
Asset change lands in its canonical repository and is re-read before any host write.
Missing shared logic is added to the asset first; no host workaround, copy or fork.
Scope linkage preserved on every projected resource.
Default deny kept for missing, stale or revoked context at every boundary touched.
The gate holds no account data.
The gate holds no account session.
Concurrent agents plus Operator edits: no silent last-writer-wins; conflicts are typed.
Cargo target under the one artifact root, owner-scoped, named in the dispatch (KB-OUT-008).
Owner cleans only its own scoped artifact folder.
UserManual updated in the same change; MANUAL_VERSION bumped where declared.
A no-context model can operate the surface from the manual alone.
Manual entries are code-truthful and self-consistency tested.

s1_narrow_build_and_receipt_decision_202.recorded_by: ORCHESTRATOR (Codex), GUI dependency specialist and separate adversarial readback
s1_narrow_build_and_receipt_decision_202.decision: S1 uses one standalone shell-gate crate, manifest/lock, README and one scoped test target under the authorized gate path. No dependency on the shell, device, asset or integration seams in S1. The single backend coder coordinates with the GUI lane and updates the approved typed startup page and UserManual version in the same commit.
s1_narrow_build_and_receipt_decision_202.receipt: Expose shell-gate --receipt <path> and judge a real headless invocation. Report native machine architecture separately from toolchain/build architecture and only package identifiers supported by the current lock or source. The eleven acceptance case statuses remain NOT_RUN. Invalid invocation or write must fail. Named feature checks remain with their later S10 scope.
s1_narrow_build_and_receipt_decision_202.proof: For the S1 static proof, independently bind successful locked x64 cargo tree normal dependency output to the exact candidate manifest and lock, target and exit. Reject absent, empty, malformed, wrong-root and banned-transitive closure input. Retain the contract's API source scan and exact implementer compile with matching before/after input digest.
s1_narrow_build_and_receipt_decision_202.limits: S1 can prove the standalone static and receipt surfaces only. The integrated AC213-1 and operator-deferred real x64 desktop proof remain unexecuted. No source edits or product tests for this record.
